The k bits are randomly distributed throughout the entire array. When the filter is larger than the CPU cache, each bit access could result in a cache miss, so a lookup may wait on memory k times.

Unsure uses a blocked Bloom filter 2 . The bit array is divided into 512-bit blocks, each matching the size of a CPU cache line. When you add or check an item, it is hashed once: part of the hash selects a block, and the rest selects k bits within that block. items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

Japanese workers dealing with the impacts of Microsoft 's ongoing 365 outage have reportedly taken to analog measures, including using fax machines to deal with the ongoing blackout, the Japan Times reports. An outage that has now lasted nearly 24 hours was still going on Friday when employees turned up to work.

The downtime has meant businesses reliant on Microsoft 365 are unable to use Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, with workplaces hit with error messages and blank screens, forced to reschedule meetings or delay work. For some, the outage has proven a respite from Japan's notoriously workaholic culture. "I couldn’t open Outlook and panicked … I got in touch with my boss and was told to stay home," one person reported on X, while another remarked that the only task they could carry out at work was to clean the coffee machine in the production room.

But while some employees and companies are throwing in the towel and calling it an early weekend, others are taking a novel, more analog approach. "Microsoft’s server glitch has made it impossible to get any work done since this morning. I guess phones and fax machines really are unbeatable. … We’re going full analog!" one user claimed. The report cites another employee who confirmed that their company was switching to fax machines to send the regular updates the company normally sends out as PDFs. "Analog is strong," they rejoiced.

Some 78% of Japanese companies rely on Microsoft for their digital infrastructure. The outage began on Thursday, with mass disruption to Outlook, Teams, Copilot, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 as a whole. It's a saga impacting entire sectors, including UK health care, businesses, travel, and transport.

Microsoft's latest update said it was seeing "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe, while the situation in America was improving, but warned some users may still experience intermittent issues. The company has also denied rumblings that the outage was caused by a cybersecurity breach. The outage has even caused some companies, such as Switzerland's luxury Richemont (Cartier) outfit, to delay giving their latest earnings report.

items.title: A Family Tree of Software Job Titles
items.content:
For a few years I was ‘Head of DevOps’. Before I got that job title I’d done much the same work under other names, and since then I’ve watched the same work get called SRE, and then it seemed to morph towards platform engineering. If you’ve been in this industry for any length of time you’ll have seen titles come and go like this, and you might have wondered where they all came from.

So I (with the help of Mr Claude) built this family tree of software job titles, from the 1940s to now.

It’s here: ianmiell.github.io/sw-job-title-family-tree

There are 104 titles, from ‘Computer’ (a person, not a machine) at the top to ‘AI Agent / Context Engineer’ at the bottom.

Time runs from top to bottom, in five-year rows. The titles sit in seven coloured columns by family:

A solid arrow means the title grew out of its parent. A dashed arrow means influence, or a common career move. Landmark titles are in bold.

On the site you can click a family to see just that column (here’s Data & AI ), or click a title to get its history, background and connections (here’s SRE ).

The whole thing is one Graphviz file and one JSON file of descriptions. Each title is one line in the .dot file, and the picture is rendered with:

$ dot -Tsvg job_title_family_tree.dot -o job_title_family_tree.svg

Adding a title is three small edits: a node in its family’s column, an entry in the row for its five-year period, and its parent arrows.

A word on the dates. They’re roughly when a title became common , not its first recorded use, and they’re my best estimates, not sourced citations. Some are well known (SRE at Google in 2003, ‘DevOps’ coined in 2009, ‘Data Scientist’ in 2008). Plenty are a ‘c.’ and a shrug.

Drawing it out made a few patterns hard to miss.

1) Coding Started Out as the Clerical Bit

In 1947, Goldstine and von Neumann’s ‘Planning and Coding of Problems’ split the work of using a computer in two: mathematicians planned the problem, and coders translated the plan into machine instructions. Coding was treated as lower-status clerical work, and much of it was done by women.

It turned out that coding eventually became the hard, creative part, and the coder merged into the programmer.

Go back further and it’s stranger still. Several of the first ENIAC programmers were recruited from the Army’s human computers, people whose job was to compute by hand. So the job gave its name to the machine, and its people to programming.

2) Titles Break Apart, Then Join Back Up

The webmaster turned up around 1993, and was often a single person who wrote the HTML, ran the webserver (often a box under a desk), answered the email, and kept the site up (sometimes by kicking it, more often by plugging it back in after kicking it).

By the mid-2000s the title had all but gone, as it was unfashionably ancient. The code went to web developers, the servers to sysadmins, and the content to editors and designers.

Then the web developer split into front-end and back-end around 2005, and the two joined back up again as ‘full-stack’ around 2008.

This is the centralisation/distribution see-saw I’ve written about before , playing out in job titles.

The prompt engineer made headlines in 2023 with a few eye-wateringly well-paid job listings. As the models got better, the skill became part of other jobs, and on the tree it gets absorbed into the AI engineer almost as soon as it appears.

The scrum master is a slower version of the same story: demand peaked in the 2010s, and many organisations have since folded it back into engineering management or delivery roles.

The newest title on the tree is the ‘AI Agent / Context Engineer’ (c. 2025). The description for it currently says “time will tell whether it stays a separate title”. I’m not taking bets.

‘Systems Engineer’ is two different jobs on the tree. At IBM in the 1960s it was a pre-sales role, working with customers to design installations and get them running. In the 1990s, thanks largely to Microsoft’s MCSE…

items.title: Someone's impersonating this blog
items.summary: security
items.content:
I was googling the name of my website, as one does occasionally, and was surprised to see a link to one of my blog posts on mataroa.site . At first I figured it was just an alternate domain name for mataroa.blog , but no, when you type mataroa.site into your browser, it shows you my blog . It's the only thing that's hosted there.

My next thought was that someone bought me a URL, but that can't be the case either: using a custom domain on mataroa requires a premium account, which I don't have. For anything but a plain redirect, I would have needed to set up the A record my end.

I then realized that the version of my blog on that site doesn't have the latest post . The most recent update on the homepage is my Aug 21 entry . When you scroll down and start clicking some of the older links, you get 404 pages. You also get a 404 if you try to post a comment, load the RSS feed or view standalone pages like the AI statement .

Someone scraped my blog and created a website to impersonate me. They're also impersonating mataroa , since using the name implies some sort of official connection.

They're re-hosting the stolen images on their own server, and they all have a watermark. Bizarrely, the watermark is mattbee.mataroa.blog , my real URL. I assume this is to somehow make it seem legitimate, like it's an officially-sanctioned mirror, but I don't know who they think is going to care. It's not like they're stealing from a site with name recognition.

When you view the source of a blog post, it's identical to the rendered HTML except that there are two Cloudflare scripts at the bottom, one to obfuscate the mailto: link in the footer (which doesn't work 1 ) and one for analytics.

When you view the source of the index, there's a hidden link at the bottom to a Chinese github.io page for a website cloning tool.

I have no idea why I was targeted for impersonation. It should be obvious this isn't a high-value website. 2 It's a personal blog where I write what's relevant to me, and that rarely overlaps with anything other people care about. If the subject matter didn't tip them off, it should be clear from the 0 comments on most posts that this is not an enterprise ripe for monetization.

If they just wanted a fake blog to scam adsense, surely a large language model would happily spew out more SEO-friendly slop than anything I have to offer. If their goal was to leech off the popularity of mataroa, why not impersonate one of the blogs with multiple front-page appearances on the orange website? Surely they have more SEO juice than me. Nothing about this makes any sense.

Anyway, the URL is registered with Namecheap, so I sent them an abuse report . I have no idea if they'll act on it. They don't seem to have a good track record of giving a shit unless the content is actually hosted with them.

It's hosted with Cloudflare, and the abuse reporting form they insist you use straight-up doesn't work . Click "Submit an abuse report" and it'll take you to a completely blank page. Very encouraging.

I'd have to dox myself to do a DMCA takedown, and I don't have the legal resources to do anything when it gets ignored. So if neither evil corporation cares to do anything, I guess I can just get fucked. I figure the best thing I can do to protect myself is document everything here. If you see a link to mataroa.site , it's not affiliated with me or mataroa. It seems like it isn't set up to scam people or distribute malware at the moment, but it probably will in the future. Be careful.

The index page also has a meta tag with a verification code for mitgo.com , a fake-looking website with some word salad identifying it as some kind of ad/SEO scamming platform or service. Will try to investigate this further.

It does, I had just forgotten to enable javascript.  ↩

Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 2: Yet another Instagram account-takeover trick is reportedly being abused, this time involving Meta’s AI chatbot. Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 1: A new exploit, which is even worse than this one is currently doing rounds on telegram. Details unknown at this time. Unpatched at the time of writing.

New Instagram Unpatched Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Allegedly, the new method is via Facebook recovery. Apparently, prompting Meta AI to turn on “Development Mode” and attaching proof of account compromise along with email works. More details awaited.

There’s a version of this story where it reads like a hypothetical from a conference talk. An AI agent with elevated backend privileges. A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

A logical flaw in Meta’s AI-powered Instagram account recovery assistant let attackers bypass two-factor authentication entirely not by cracking a code or intercepting an SMS, but by talking the chatbot into doing the work for them. High-value “OG” Instagram handles worth hundreds of thousands of dollars were stolen and resold on Telegram within minutes of each compromise. The dormant Obama White House account got hijacked. Prominent researchers woke up locked out of their own profiles.

Instagram has notoriously poor human support infrastructure. Recovering a locked account – especially a high-value one can take weeks of back-and-forth with an automated ticketing system. Meta’s solution was to deploy a conversational AI layer to handle common recovery workflows: relinking a lost email address, triggering a password reset, verifying account ownership. items.title: China Switches on World's Biggest Example of New, Cheap Green Energy Storage
items.content:
Home All News Business China Switches on World’s Biggest Example of New, Cheap Green Energy Storage

Qinghai 60MW Liquid Air Energy Storage Project – credit, China Green Development Investment Group

The world’s largest demonstration plant for a new kind of renewable energy storage is up and running in the west of the China.

Called liquid-air energy storage (LAES) the plant uses renewable electricity to compress air to extreme densities until it turns to liquid. It can then be rapidly released to power a turbine and discharge that green energy back into the grid.

China has received numerous plaudits for its rapid adoption of renewable energy at both scale and speed, and this new facility in Qinghai Province brings in a key missing element to the renewable build-out: grid-scale battery storage for when the Sun isn’t shining and the wind isn’t blowing.

Not that either of those happen very often in Qinghai, which encompasses parts of the Tibetan Plateau, and Mongolia-like grasslands and desert, where both sun and wind are famously relentless.

Described as “the world’s largest grid-connected liquid-air energy storage facility by both rated power and energy capacity,” the facility is rated at 600 megawatt-hours, and will substantially back up the renewable contribution to the regional power grid by providing 10 hours of continual power supply when necessary. Additionally, it was built with its own solar farm, rated at 250MW.

LAES works by turning ordinary air into a liquid, keeping that liquid in insulated tanks, and then converting it back into electricity when needed.

When electricity is plentiful, it powers machinery that draws in air, compresses it and cools it to extremely low temperatures of around -190°C. At this point, the air becomes a liquid, taking up far less space than it did as a gas.

When power is needed, the liquid air is pumped to high pressure and warmed. As it warms, it rapidly expands back into a gas and can be used to spin a turbine connected to an electricity generator, sending power back to the grid.

A cool party trick is how the system utilizes the excess heat and cold: it stores both for heating and cooling the air as needed, reducing energy consumption and environmental disturbance.

ALSO CHECK OUT: New Solar Tech Makes Desalinating Seawater Cheaper Than Producing Bottled Water

Developed by state-owned China Green Development Investment Group (CGDG) in cooperation with the Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), it has 20% more capacity than the first commercial-scale LAES project in the US which was slated for construction in northern Vermont.

The development was undertaken by Highview Power and Encore Renewable Energy, and if built will help solar and wind gain a larger purchase in a high-demand energy district known as the Sheffield-Highgate Export Interface.

SCALING UP RENEWABLE ENERGY: World’s Largest Battery to Revolutionize Renewable Energy Storage in Maine with ‘Reverse Rusting’

Rated at 400MWh, it could deliver grid-scale renewable electricity for 8 hours straight, helping to reduce the use of fossil fuels when the interface is overloaded, which according to Recharge News happens frequently.

Cost comparisons with standard lithium-ion battery storage systems are apparently very appealing, with LAES costing at least 33 cents on the dollar when the two systems are compared, according to financial analyst and asset management firm Lazard.

items.title: KDE is hiring a developer with a focus for Plasma Mobile!
items.content:
KDE is an international community dedicated to developing Free and Open Source Software for end users. Contributions are made by thousands of talented volunteer contributors (developers, artists, marketers, translators, documentation writers, etc.) worldwide, working on software such as a desktop environment, graphics applications, PIM apps, games, educational software, and more. KDE e.V. is the legal organization behind KDE, representing and supporting the community.

KDE e.V. is looking for a software engineer to improve KDE’s Plasma Mobile in ways that support user acquisition through growth into new hardware and software markets by addressing defects and missing features that are barriers to these objectives.

The ideal candidate is passionate about seeing KDE software pre-installed on more mobile devices and operating systems, and possesses the software development skills to develop KDE software so as to make it more likely to happen.

3+ years of experience in KDE or Qt development

Strong understanding of the underlying technologies of the KDE stack (C++, Qt, KDE Frameworks, preferably Plasma) and FOSS contribution processes

Experience working with C++ Frameworks and understanding the challenges it poses

Ability to work within an open community and gather requirements from different sources

Deep knowledge of data structures and algorithms

Experience working with free and open-source mobile operating systems or operating systems

Essential functions and responsibilities

You will take on tasks that are relevant to KDE Plasma and need attention to bring our technology forward.

Develop new and existing functionality for Qt, KDE Frameworks, relevant middleware libraries, and other parts of KDE‘s software stack in ways that are of benefit to KDE Plasma as a whole.

Work with the different KDE teams (Plasma, Frameworks, Goals, the different App teams) as well as downstream communities (Nura, Mobian, and various distributions) for Plasma Mobile to improve the user experience of KDE Plasma Mobile.

Improve the accessibility for the various applications and KDE Plasma user interface

Execute grant-funded work in line with agreed objectives and deliverables

Salary: Depending on the experience, commensurate with title and responsibilities

Please send your application, including your availability and pointers to Free Software projects you are most proud of, by email to kde-ev-board@kde.org with “KDE Software Engineer” in the subject.

Do not hesitate to contact us at the same address if you have any questions.

items.title: LinkedIn, Monster take down over 1000 fake job postings after CBC investigation
items.content:
More than 1,500 misleading job postings — offering remote work, no experience needed — have been taken down from LinkedIn and Monster after a CBC visual investigation revealed the listings funnelled unsuspecting applicants to a multi-level marketing (MLM) company that asked for money.

CBC connected a network of travel-related pages posting suspicious jobs — positions like "Work From Home Travel Planner and Virtual Customer Support Representative" — to a U.S.-based MLM called Evolution Travel. Some of the roles promised to pay up to $75,000 US per year.

In reality, there was no job and no salary.

Applicants were quickly directed to join virtual information sessions, where they were asked to pay hundreds of dollars up front, followed by a monthly subscription fee. The program promised to teach members how to make money from booking travel as an independent agent and recruiting others into the program, taking a cut of their commissions.

Exposing who’s behind fake job ads online

The companies went by names like Wanderwell Collective, Professional Travel Hub, Remote-Careers, Sky Land & Ocean Travel and Sunkissed Getaways.

The job postings made no mention of Evolution Travel or sign-up fees.

Many of the jobs did not require experience and promised to pay up to $75,000 US. (Illustration: Matthew Hoddy/CBC; LinkedIn)

"This is disgusting," said Jay Jones, a Chicago-based job listing investigator who CBC shared its findings with. "They catch you with the lure of the fake job. The money is great, [successful applicants] get to stay at home. You have to pay to get work — that's not how work works."

Misleading job postings — including ones that require payment or lead to MLMs — are strictly prohibited on platforms like LinkedIn and other job sites.

Jay Jones investigates misleading and fake jobs online. (CBC)

"It feels in so many ways that we're living in a funhouse mirror," said Vass Bednar, managing director of the Canadian Shield Institute, a public policy think-tank that focuses on economic resilience and digital sovereignty.

These postings risk "eroding confidence — confidence in the self and confidence that there is, frankly, meaningful work out there for people that is worth pursuing."

MLMs are not illegal in Canada or the U.S. However, in the U.S., companies and individuals could face fines if they are found to violate the U.S. Federal Trade Commission Act, which prohibits "unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce."

"I would consider [these job posts] misleading… and would invite enforcement by either the FTC, the state governments or other federal enforcement agencies," said William Kovacic, former FTC chairman and commissioner, with whom CBC also shared its findings.

One independent agent behind multiple travel businesses linked to misleading jobs ads CBC identified — Wanderwell Collective, Destination Knot, Aisle and Abroad, and Professional Travel Hub — was Diedre Norton. In one video posted to YouTube, Norton said she had a network of 300 recruits for Evolution Travel.

Even though Evolution Travel’s founder, David McCovy, praised her in online videos as being a top performer, Norton denied being affiliated with the program before hanging up on CBC News.

Screenshot of an online video showing Evolution founder David McCovy during a conference. (EvolutionTravelCafe/YouTube)

McCovy did not respond to CBC’s requests for comment.

A representative from Evolution Travel who only identified themselves by their title, chief operating officer, told CBC they have consistently told their independent agents not to post job ads on any platforms.

Late last month, LinkedIn took down close to 900 ads connected to Evolution Travel, saying it had removed them because they were "misleading and violated" company policy, adding "the companies behind them will no longer be able to post jobs" on the platform.

Monster took down 600 listings, saying it has "clear policies prohibiting misleading job postings…

items.title: Writing a DSL for high performance parallel programming in OxCaml
items.summary: performance, plt
items.content:
Writing a DSL for high performance parallel programming in OxCaml

The following is part of a series of posts about 2026 summer intern projects—for more,

see “What the interns have wrought, special jumbo 2026

We have a lot of performance-critical SIMD code (single-instruction, multiple-data)

running on CPUs across the firm. These are highly parallel programs where you run the same

computation across arrays of data, in our case for options pricing or for low-latency risk

checks. Because OCaml hasn’t historically exposed SIMD instructions, these programs often

involve an inner loop written in fairly esoteric C. Writing these loops requires

implementers to think carefully about hardware, and doing performance tuning, such as

modifying unroll factors or vector widths, can require major changes to the code.

Moreover, these programs are constrained to a specific instruction set. If we were to

target a different architecture or a newer processor, we’d have to rewrite the program.

For his summer internship, Sai Konkimalla built a compiler for a domain specific language

(DSL) that makes SIMD more ergonomic and widely accessible. The compiler takes advantage

of OxCaml features that were only very recently added to the

language, such as runtime metaprogramming, to enable users to write a kernel just once as

a regular-ish OxCaml function, then compile and run it on multiple architectures.

To help solve the problem of SIMD code being rather difficult to write and maintain, our

DSL uses the S P MD, or “single program , multiple data” programming model. As

opposed to SIMD intrinsics, SPMD is higher level and not tied to a specific instruction

set. We might normally think of higher-level languages as slower, but with SPMD, a higher

level of abstraction lets the compiler make better decisions about how to optimally use

the underlying hardware. This ability can lead to significantly faster code.

SPMD was popularized by CUDA (for Nvidia GPUs) and ISPC (for Intel CPUs). In this model,

you write a program describing what happens at each index of a loop, then the compiler

converts it into a parallel computation. For example, in CUDA:

__global__ void kernel ( const float * x , float * out , int n ) {

int idx = blockIdx . x * blockDim . x + threadIdx . x ;

out [ idx ] = 2 . 0 f * x [ idx ] + idx ;

Notice how there’s no loop here: you only define the loop body, and the compiler decides

how to run it. In CUDA, when you launch a kernel on a GPU, you can declare how many blocks

of threads to run and the GPU will schedule them accordingly.

In ISPC, foreach also abstracts away how the loop is actually executed:

export void kernel ( uniform float x [], uniform float out [], uniform int n ) {

In both cases, the compiler translates the code into low-level SIMD instructions. Not

specifying the exact instructions also means SPMD programs can benefit from future

hardware improvements. If we get a new, faster CPU with a different instruction set, the

SPMD compiler can seamlessly compile existing code to it.

kernel’s signature, including its output type, input types, and the dimension of the

Future work on a ppx syntax extension will make it possible to rewrite the above simply

( fun graph [ x ; scale ] [ Dim i ] -> exclave_

F32 . (( x .!( i ) *. broadcast scale .!( I32 . lit # 0 l )) +. of_i32 i ))

Note the let open (val Spmd.open_ graph) in . This brings the DSL operations which

construct a computational graph into scope. You can think of the graph value as proof

that you’re in the graph-construction phase, not the runtime of the generated program.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: Microsoft Outage Knocks Out Email for Businesses, Police, and Hospitals: The tech giant is racing to fully restore Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft 365 services following a widespread outage.
items.content:
Microsoft is still scrambling to fully restore services as a massive outage stretched into its second day, disrupting operations at governments, hospitals, and businesses around the world.

The tech giant said in a post on X Friday morning that service availability is improving, but some users may still be affected.

“Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as recovery continues,” the company said.

As of Friday morning, Microsoft’s status page still showed “ service degradation ” for both business and consumer versions of Microsoft 365. The company warned that users may be unable to access several Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook and Teams.

Microsoft said it has found no evidence that malicious activity was at fault and is continuing to investigate the underlying cause of the outage.

The problems began around noon on Thursday. In subsequent updates, Microsoft said it found that a large number of servers had unexpectedly become unavailable, “straining the remaining infrastructure.”

Microsoft subsequently determined that a process responsible for establishing secure connections was becoming overwhelmed, causing servers to stop responding. The company has since rolled out a patch to improve server stability, but has not established the underlying cause of the problem.

“We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure,” Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, said in an emailed statement to Gizmodo. “We know our customers rely on our services to get important work done every day, and regret the impact these outages had on those who depend on us. Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward.”

Meanwhile, the outage has disrupted all sorts of organizations, from major businesses to government agencies.

Shipping giant Maersk warned customers that their emails and notifications could be delayed or disrupted. Electric-truck maker Workhorse Group postponed its scheduled third-quarter earnings report and investor call to next week because of disruptions from the outage.

The outage also reportedly delayed some difficult conversations at PVH Corp., the parent company of Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger. Bloomberg reports that the company announced Thursday that it was cutting about 4% of its global workforce. However, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that some conversations with affected employees in Asia scheduled for Friday morning did not take place because of the outage, leaving workers uncertain about their futures.

Over in Japan, government ministries were forced to post paper notices to notify journalists of their schedules.

Some National Health Service hospitals in the United Kingdom reported email disruptions. Guy’s and St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust said its services were operating and procedures were continuing as scheduled. However, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that some procedures elsewhere had to be rescheduled.

Back in the U.S., the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said Thursday night that the outage was disrupting its email and other communication platforms. Meanwhile, Colorado’s Arapahoe County Sheriff’s Office warned that the outage was affecting online bond payments for people held at its detention facility and must now be paid in person. The City of Austin also reported that employees were unable to send or receive emails Thursday, while other local governments issued similar notices. Several colleges, including Stanford University and George Mason University , also reported disruptions.

items.content_ko: 마이크로소프트 장애는 목요일 정오쯤 시작되었다. 회사는 다수의 서버가 예기치 않게 사용할 수 없게 되어 남은 인프라에 부담이 가중되었다고 밝혔고, 이후 보안 연결을 설정하는 프로세스가 과부하에 걸려 서버가 멈춘 것으로 확인했다. 금요일 오전 기준 상태 페이지에는 비즈니스용과 소비자용 Microsoft 365 모두 ‘서비스 저하(service degradation)’가 표시되었고, Outlook과 Teams 등 여러 서비스 이용이 어려울 수 있다고 경고되었다. 회사는 악의적 활동이 원인이라는 증거는 찾지 못했다고 밝혔다. 원문이 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: As Ottawa Gambles on AI, Canadians Live with the Mistakes | The Walrus
items.content:
Splash of Rain, Pexels / iStock / Ana Luisa O.J.

L ast year, Kémy Adé , a post-doctoral research fellow and guest teacher at McMaster University, applied for permanent residence to Canada. Her application made her, in the words of her immigration lawyer, “a prime candidate.” Adé is a health scientist specializing in immunology of aging—precisely the highly skilled immigrant Canada competes to attract.

Nearly half of Canadian public servants admit to frequently using AI in their work

Federal departments use AI without common binding rules or safeguards

Low regulation on AI usage can lead to judgment errors that shape life-changing decisions

But she was rejected. In its refusal letter, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada pointed to job duties that did not match the experience Adé had claimed, such as wiring control circuits and assembling panels used to operate machinery and robots. None of those duties, however, were hers. Someone or something—or both—got it all wrong.

As the Toronto Star reported, the letter disclosed that generative artificial intelligence had been used in the processing. Like other federal departments, IRCC has adopted AI to vet applications faster, filtering out those that raise flags from those that require less stringent review. IRCC says that a human always gets the final say, but “I cannot comprehend how any human being could make this decision,” Adé’s lawyer told the Star . “Somehow, it hallucinated my client’s job description.”

Adé’s experience is a glimpse of a much larger, scarier—and murkier—experiment under way across Ottawa. AI’s footprint has grown exponentially since ChatGPT’s introduction in 2022, with more than 80 percent of companies globally using the technology. That ubiquity puts enormous pressure on leaders to keep pace. Mark Carney’s government isn’t shirking. As it splashes out on public-facing AI investments and policy, framing it as a necessity for future economic success, federal departments and agencies are availing themselves of the technology for everything from translation to detecting national security threats.

But while private industry has a responsibility to the public at a consumer level, the federal government’s role is different. A corporation can adopt AI to maximize profits first and protect people as a secondary consideration. The federal government can’t, or at least shouldn’t. It is responsible to citizens, and those citizens might rightfully expect the standards to be a lot higher. In theory, they are. But in practice? Well.

For all its vaunted miracles—it can automate routine work, accelerate research, code—AI remains one of the most fallible tools we have. Ontario’s auditor general reported in 2026 that approved AI scribes fabricated patient information in 45 percent of cases, recorded wrong meds 60 percent of the time, and missed key mental health details 85 percent of the time.

The risk is clear. And yet it is astonishing how little clarity there is in how it is being used by federal employees. Some of that adoption is formally declared and governed. Much is not. Any visibility—which tools, for what purposes, on what data—varies by department or may not exist at all. This opacity is partly structural. Canada’s federal government is balkanized, with each department effectively operating as a separate kingdom. Each deputy minister may have their own chief information officer and their own appetite for AI. There is no central strategy to constrain these things and channel them down the same path. One person with knowledge of the overall AI rollout told me that, from one department to the next, “it’s really hard to say what’s happening inside the stack.”

In cases where the government admits AI was involved, as it did with Adé, it has offered assurances that a human reviewed the work and made the final call. But those assurances rarely hold up. Then, there’s the black box nature of the technology itself. Commercial confidentiality rules protect…

items.summary_ko: 맥매스터대 박사후 연구원 Kémy Adé는 캐나다 영주권을 신청했지만 거절당했다. 거절 서한은 그가 하지 않은 업무를 근거로 들었고, 이 과정에 생성형 AI가 사용됐다고 밝혔다. 기사는 공공 부문의 AI 사용에 공통 규칙과 안전장치가 부족하다는 점을 짚는다.
items.content_ko: 맥매스터대 박사후 연구원이자 객원 강사인 Kémy Adé는 캐나다 영주권을 신청했지만 거절당했다. 이민·난민·시민권부(IRCC)의 거절 서한은 그의 경력과 맞지 않는 업무로 제어 회로 배선과 기계·로봇 조작 패널 조립을 들었다. 그러나 그 업무들은 모두 그의 것이 아니었다. Toronto Star에 따르면 이 서한은 신청 처리 과정에 생성형 AI가 사용됐다는 사실도 밝혔다. IRCC는 신청서를 더 빨리 심사하기 위해 AI를 도입했다. 기사에 따르면 캐나다 공무원의 거의 절반이 업무에서 AI를 자주 쓴다고 인정했으며, 연방 부처들은 공통의 구속력 있는 규칙이나 안전장치 없이 AI를 사용하고 있다. 규제가 느슨하면 인생을 바꾸는 결정에서 판단 오류가 생길 수 있다.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-127115 📢 Source: Wordfence 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False The BuddyForms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'buddyforms_form_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.10.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping.
